title: The U.S. Capital for Exactly One Day — and Almost Nobody Noticed
summary:
Quick — name every U.S. capital city. Washington, D.C., sure. Philadelphia, yes. But Lancaster, Pennsylvania? For exactly one day in 1777, this city was the capital of the United States.

Here's what happened. It was September 1777, during the American Revolution. The British army was marching toward Philadelphia, where Congress was meeting. A messenger named Alexander Hamilton — yes, that Hamilton — sent an urgent warning: "If Congress have not yet left Philadelphia, they ought to do it immediately without fail."

So more than two dozen delegates grabbed important government papers and ran. They took a sneaky route, traveling nearly 180 miles even though the direct road was only 88 miles, to avoid being caught.

On September 27, they met in Lancaster's courthouse for just a few hours. Then they decided: nope, the British could get here too. So they moved again, to York.

Lancaster's one-day reign was over. Today, it's one of only nine cities that have ever been the U.S. capital. "That makes Lancaster a member of a very exclusive club," says author Adam Zurn. The city even throws a party every year called Capital Day.
why_it_matters: It reminds us that even small places can be part of big history, and that the country we know today was once messy, moving, and unsure of itself.

background_read: The American Revolution was the war in which the 13 American colonies fought to break free from Britain, and during it the young government had to keep moving to stay safe.
Back then, Congress was a meeting of delegates sent by each colony, and they carried the important government papers with them when they fled.
Today the U.S. capital is Washington, D.C., but the capital moved around a lot in the early years — Lancaster is one of only nine cities that have ever held the title.
Article_Structure: WHO: More than two dozen delegates of Congress, warned by a messenger named Alexander Hamilton
WHAT: They made Lancaster, Pennsylvania the U.S. capital for one day, then quickly moved again to York
WHERE: Lancaster's courthouse, after fleeing Philadelphia because the British army was coming
WHY: They needed a safe place to meet and keep the government running during the American Revolution

perspectives.description: They say their city belongs in the story of America and celebrate it every year with Capital Day.
They point out that meeting for only a few hours is a very short time to really count as a capital, so the title is a bit of a technicality.
They see it as proof that in a war, governments sometimes have to grab their papers and run wherever they can be safe.
